4433               	;
4434               	; 	' NO ALPHA LOCK CALIBRATION, AND THERE USED TO BE ONE.
4435               	; 	'
4436               	; 	' The premise was that ALPHA LOCK shares a line with the joystick's
4437               	; 	' VERTICAL axis, so a latched key reports a direction that is never
4438               	; 	' released -- fatal here, where down is the duck and up is the lift. The
4439               	; 	' guard sampled the axis for forty frames before listening and then
4440               	; 	' ignored any direction that had been held for essentially all of them.
4441               	; 	'
4442               	; 	' IT WAS REMOVED BECAUSE THE PREMISE DOES NOT HOLD UP.
4443               	; 	'
4444               	; 	'   * CLAUDE.md claimed every other game here dodged the problem by not
4445               	; 	'     reading up/down. EIGHT of them do read it -- Adventire, Astiroids,
4446               	; 	'     HardHatMack, Ms. Pac-Man, RallyX, Structris, UFO, Bust-A-Bobble --
4447               	; 	'     and not one has a calibration or has ever shown the fault.
4448               	; 	'   * It never fired on the machine this is developed on: the notice it
4449               	; 	'     prints when it detects a stuck axis has never appeared.
4450               	; 	'   * The original evidence was that the game "came up and would not
4451               	; 	'     start" -- and the first version BLOCKED until the axis cleared. That
4452               	; 	'     symptom is indistinguishable from the several input bugs since found
4453               	; 	'     and fixed for real: keys arriving at a screen that was not listening
4454               	; 	'     yet. The diagnosis was probably one of those.
4455               	; 	'
4456               	; 	' It also cost two bugs of its own: forty frames of a drawn but deaf title
4457               	; 	' screen, which swallowed the first digit of 8-3-8, and a wrong theory
4458               	; 	' about keyboard noise that led to a filter which ate real presses.
4459               	; 	'
4460               	; 	' If a stuck axis ever does appear it will be obvious -- the player will
4461               	; 	' duck or ride the lift without asking -- and the guard is in the history.
4462               	;
4463               	; title_input:
4464               cvb_TITLE_INPUT
4465               	; 	' THE PROMPT IS PRINTED HERE, NOT WITH THE REST OF THE TITLE, because
4466               	; 	' this is the moment the game starts listening -- and it is a whole
4467               	; 	' second after the title appears.
4468               	; 	'
4469               	; 	' title_draw runs early on purpose (DESIGN.md 0d-nonies) so the screen
4470               	; 	' arrives instead of filling in, but setup_rest, init_tables and the
4471               	; 	' ALPHA LOCK sample all run AFTER it. For about a second the title is up,
4472               	; 	' finished, and completely deaf. A player types 8-3-8 into that window and
4473               	; 	' the first digit lands in nothing -- then a following 3-8 completes the
4474               	; 	' code, because the 8 they typed second is still standing as state. That
4475               	; 	' is exactly how it was reported, twice, and it is not noise: it is the
4476               	; 	' screen lying about being ready.
4477               	; 	'
4478               	; 	' RallyX and Bust-A-Bobble never showed this because they draw their

4507               	; 	' THE MARQUEE CHASES WHILE THE TITLE WAITS.
4508               	; 	'
4509               	; 	' ONLY TWO CHARACTERS CHANGE PER STEP. At any moment exactly one of the
4510               	; 	' four lamps is blank; a step lights the one that was blank and blanks the
4511               	; 	' next one round. Redefining all four would be twice the work for the same
4512               	; 	' picture.
4513               	; 	'
4514               	; 	' IT IS BELOW THE INPUT READS, deliberately. This loop's history is input
4515               	; 	' bugs -- a screen that was drawn but not listening, a keypress eaten by a
4516               	; 	' stability filter -- so nothing that is merely decoration goes in front of
4517               	; 	' the polling. A dropped frame of animation is invisible; a dropped
4518               	; 	' keypress is what took three sessions to find.
4519               	; 	' `bphs` IS WHICH LAMP IS DARK, and a step is: light that one, move on,
4520               	; 	' darken the next. The character number is arithmetic rather than a
4521               	; 	' four-way branch -- DEFINE CHAR takes an expression, so the whole chase
4522               	; 	' is two calls and no `IF` ladder. The ladder version was eight DEFINE
4523               	; 	' CHARs across four branches and cost about three hundred bytes for the
4524               	; 	' same picture.
4525               	; 	'
4526               	; 	' TWO CALLS, NOT FIVE. Lighting all four and then darkening one is the
4527               	; 	' same result and reads more simply, but two separate DEFINEs can have a
4528               	; 	' vblank between them, so the sign would show ALL lamps lit for a frame
4529               	; 	' every step -- a flash rather than a chase. Only ever changing the two
4530               	; 	' lamps that actually change cannot do that.
4531               	; 	bfr = bfr - 1
4532 B22E D020  34 	movb @cvb_BFR,r0
     B230 2086

4549               	; 		' QUEUED, NOT BLANKED -- AND THIS IS WHAT MADE THE TITLE FLASH.
4550               	; 		'
4551               	; 		' nes_def turns rendering OFF and waits for a vblank the NMI
4552               	; 		' therefore never services, so the game's own WAIT then waits for
4553               	; 		' the one after: about two frames with the picture switched off.
4554               	; 		' Twice a marquee step, for ever, on the one screen the player

4596               	; 		' A SECOND STAGING AREA, AND THIS IS THE WHOLE MARQUEE BUG.
4597               	; 		'
4598               	; 		' nes_escd does NOT copy anything. It builds the tile into the RAM
4599               	; 		' buffer `#nesb` and hands the NMI a five-byte descriptor holding a
4600               	; 		' POINTER to it; the copy happens at the next vblank. Both marquee
4601               	; 		' writes happen in the same pass, so with one buffer the darken call
4602               	; 		' overwrote the staged LIT bytes before the NMI had read either --
4603               	; 		' and then BOTH descriptors copied bulb_off.
4604               	; 		'
4605               	; 		' So every step darkened two lamps and lit none, and the sign walked
4606               	; 		' itself out: "it animates a little bit and goes out". Nothing fails,
4607               	; 		' because both writes are perfectly valid and land exactly where they
4608               	; 		' were addressed -- they just carry the same sixteen bytes.
4609               	; 		'
4610               	; 		' The lit call staged at nesb(0); this one stages sixteen bytes up.
4611               	; 		' nesb is 96 bytes for the escalator's six characters and the
4612               	; 		' escalator never runs on the title screen, so the room is free. The
4613               	; 		' pointer is put back immediately: esc_tick stages at offset 0 and
4614               	; 		' would otherwise write its six characters one tile off.
4615               	; 		#nesb = #nesb + 16
4616               	; 		#nsrc = VARPTR bulb_off(0)

4744               	;
4745               	; 	' 8-3-8 IS EDGE-TRIGGERED AND ANY STRAY DIGIT RESETS IT (see title_wait).
4746               	; 	'
4747               	; 	' It used to read cont1.key raw every pass and test only for the digit it
4748               	; 	' wanted next. That worked -- but only because 8-3-8 ALTERNATES, so holding
4749               	; 	' 8 cannot advance past the first step. It is an accident of the sequence
4750               	; 	' rather than a design, and it had two costs: 8,5,3,9,8 opened this page as
4751               	; 	' readily as 8,3,8, and a key that READS as held for many frames got a free
4752               	; 	' walk through the state machine.
4753               	; 	'
4754               	; 	' That second one is not hypothetical on this machine. ALPHA LOCK shorts a
4755               	; 	' keyboard line -- and Classic99 defaults to invertcaps, so it reads DOWN
4756               	; 	' with the host's Caps Lock UP -- and this page was reached twice from
4757               	; 	' single keypresses while testing an unrelated change.
4758               	; 	'
4759               	; 	' The reset is the DEFAULT rather than a test for a particular wrong digit:
4760               	; 	' Bust-A-Bobble resets only on a stray 3 and still lets 8,5,3,8 through.

5469               	;
5470               	; 	' ======================================================================
5471               	; 	' DRAWING THE STORE -- four blits, once per screen crossing
5472               	; 	' ======================================================================
5473               	; 	' This is the whole cost of the flip, and it is paid on a discrete event
5474               	; 	' rather than every frame. RallyX's pan repaints 576 chars every time the
5475               	; 	' camera moves one cell; this repaints 640 about once every two seconds
5476               	; 	' of running.
5477               	; 	' SPRITES OFF BEFORE THE BLIT, NOT AFTER IT. This routine WAITs between
5478               	; 	' bands -- one band a frame, because a burst of VDP writes past a few
5479               	; 	' dozen in one frame is silently dropped -- so painting the new screen
5480               	; 	' takes several frames, and for all of them the OLD screen's actors and
5481               	; 	' obstacles were still sitting on top of it. Following Harry through a
5482               	; 	' seam showed him and every cart from the floor he had just left,
5483               	; 	' standing on a shop that was assembling itself underneath them.
5484               	; 	'
5485               	; 	' They are put back by the normal draw on the same pass, so the crossing
5486               	; 	' reads as a cut rather than as a dissolve with ghosts in it.
5487               	; 	' EACH BAND IS FINISHED BEFORE THE FRAME IT IS DRAWN IN ENDS, and the
5488               	; 	' bands go TOP DOWN. Both halves of that matter.
5489               	; 	'
5490               	; 	' The blit paints the template -- shelves, pillars and all -- and the
5491               	; 	' radios and prizes then take out the fixtures they stand in. Those two
5492               	; 	' used to be four frames apart: all four bands blitted with a WAIT
5493               	; 	' between them, and only afterwards the clearing. So every screen change
5494               	; 	' showed its counters and beams for several frames and then erased them,
5495               	; 	' which reads as the shop flickering rather than as it being drawn.
5496               	; 	'
5497               	; 	' TOP DOWN because a band's beam tops are stamped into the SLAB ROW OF
5498               	; 	' THE BAND ABOVE. Going bottom-up, band 1's blit would paint over the
5499               	; 	' beam tops band 0 had just put there. Going top-down the band above is
5500               	; 	' always already drawn, so everything a band needs -- its own cells and
5501               	; 	' the row it borrows overhead -- is final by the time its WAIT arrives.
5502               	; 	'
5503               	; 	' `3 - dq` rather than `FOR dlv = 3 TO 0 STEP -1`: dlv is an unsigned
5504               	; 	' byte, so counting down past zero wraps to 255 and the loop never ends
5505               	; 	' (CLAUDE.md 3A).
5506               	; draw_screen:
5507               cvb_DRAW_SCREEN
5508               	; 	#if NES
5509               	; 	' AND BLACK BACK FOR THE STORE -- see the note in title_draw. Index 0 is
5510               	; 	' the universal backdrop, so the dark blue the title sets would otherwise
5511               	; 	' tint every outline, the HUD row and the ground under the scanner.
5512               	; 	'
5513               	; 	' A DARK BLUE BACKDROP WAS TRIED HERE, to give the sunset a fourth band
5514               	; 	' (see nes_inkmap in assets/nes_chr.asm). It works, and it costs the
5515               	; 	' escalator, the radar ground and every black outline in the store, all of
5516               	; 	' which ride on index 0. One sky band is not worth the store's line work.
5517               	; 	PALETTE 0,15			' black

5578               	; 		#if NES
5579               	; 		#ddst = #ddst + 96		' three rows down -- see the overscan note
5580               	; 		' ONE ROW A FRAME, AND THIS IS WHY THREE BANDS IN FOUR LOST THEIR
5581               	; 		' LAST TWO ROWS. The NMI copies PPUBUF into the PPU during vblank
5582               	; 		' and its copy loop DOES NOT STOP WHEN VBLANK ENDS -- it runs to
5583               	; 		' the end of the descriptor whatever the raster is doing, and a
5584               	; 		' PPUDATA write outside vblank is discarded by the hardware.
5585               	; 		'
5586               	; 		' NTSC gives about 2273 CPU cycles of vblank, OAM DMA takes 513 of
5587               	; 		' them, and the copy costs roughly 14 a byte: about a hundred bytes
5588               	; 		' get through. A 32x5 band is 160, so the last sixty-odd vanished
5589               	; 		' -- three whole rows arrived, the fourth stopped eight or nine
5590               	; 		' cells in, and the floor bar and the air row above it were simply
5591               	; 		' never there. Measured on screen as `#########.......`, on every
5592               	; 		' band whose blit did not happen to start early.
5593               	; 		'
5594               	; 		' A row is 32 bytes, which fits with room to spare. This costs four
5595               	; 		' extra frames per band at round start and nothing during play.
5596               	; 		SCREEN stor_tpl,#dsrc,#ddst,32,3,32
5597               	; 		WAIT
5598               	; 		#dsrc = #dsrc + 96
5599               	; 		#ddst = #ddst + 96

5653               	;
5654               	; 	' A SUPPORT BEAM HAS TO REACH THE FLOOR IT HOLDS UP, AND THAT FLOOR IS
5655               	; 	' NOT IN ITS OWN BAND. A beam fills its band's four air rows, so its top
5656               	; 	' pixel sits under the slab row of the band ABOVE -- and a slab row is
5657               	; 	' five pixels of bar over three of green (see SLAB), so the beam stopped
5658               	; 	' three pixels short of the bar on every storey. It read as a beam that
5659               	; 	' misses the floor, which is exactly what it was.
5660               	; 	'
5661               	; 	' It cannot be drawn into either template. The beam belongs to the band
5662               	; 	' below and the row belongs to the band above, and the two templates are
5663               	; 	' chosen independently per screen, so no template knows both. So the
5664               	; 	' band blits go down first and the tops are stamped afterwards, from a
5665               	; 	' per-template column table -- the same shape as the escalator's head cap.
5666               	; 	'
5667               	; 	' Bands 0 and 1 only. Band 2's top row is the ROOF DECK, which is grey
5668               	; 	' over grey with no green to bridge, and the roof itself has no band
5669               	; 	' above it at all.
5670               	; 	' BANDS 0 TO 2 -- ALL THREE SHOPPING FLOORS. It used to stop at 1,
5671               	; 	' because band 2's ceiling is the ROOF DECK and the deck had no green
5672               	; 	' under it: a beam there already ran straight into grey and needed
5673               	; 	' nothing. Giving the roof its three green rows (so the lift shaft stops

6302               	; 			' from one edge, so the obstacles start at the OTHER edge and

6304               	; 			' ONCOMING stream, never a set of backs he has to catch up

6313               	; 			' THAT DISTANCE IS SET BY THE JUMP.

6316               	; 			' the placement table plus a constant -- so the gap between

6325               	; 			' closes on an oncoming hazard at (KWALK64 + its speed)/64

6327               	; 			' eats 82 px of closing distance at the fastest hazard. At

6445               	; 			' THE BALL IS ON THE GROUND WHEN HE GETS TO IT.
6446               	; 			'
6447               	; 			' The bounce phase used to be `lx AND 31` -- a byte out of
6448               	; 			' the placement table, which is to say arbitrary. Run onto
6449               	; 			' a screen and the first ball might be at the bottom of its
6450               	; 			' arc, where a jump clears it, or at the top, where it has
6451               	; 			' to be ducked, and nothing on the way in told you which.
6452               	; 			' Sometimes you could keep running and jump it; sometimes
6453               	; 			' the same approach at the same speed could not be jumped
6454               	; 			' at all. That is not difficulty, it is a coin toss.
6455               	; 			'
6456               	; 			' So the phase is worked BACKWARDS from the meeting. He
6457               	; 			' closes 4 px a pass and the ball 2, so they meet in
6458               	; 			' (gap / 6) passes; the phase advances one a pass and wraps
6459               	; 			' at 32, so seeding it with the NEGATIVE of that lands it on
6460               	; 			' phase 0 -- the ground -- exactly as they arrive.
6461               	; 			'
6462               	; 			' The gap is the same either way round: he enters at one
6463               	; 			' wall and the ball starts `stag` in from the other, so it
6464               	; 			' is 232 - stag whichever direction the floor runs.
6465               	; 			'
6466               	; 			' It stays forgiving rather than exact. The arc is flat near
6467               	; 			' the bottom, so anything within eight passes either side is
6468               	; 			' still under the jump; and it only holds for an unbroken
6469               	; 			' run, which is the case the player is entitled to read off
6470               	; 			' the screen. Duck, stop or take a hit and everything after
6471               	; 			' is out of step again -- which is the game.
6472               	; 			' obp is a BALL-only field: upd_obst reads it under an
6473               	; 			' IF uk = OB_BALL and nothing else touches it, and every
6474               	; 			' ball has it computed below. It was seeded here from a

7231               	;
7232               	; 	' ONE CELL OF THE DOORWAY, from its column (ccl 0-3), its band row
7233               	; 	' (crw 0-3) and the door state (cst). Four columns and four rows, so
7234               	; 	' sixteen cells, and the three interesting things about a cell are all
7235               	; 	' edges: column 0 and column 3 carry the JAMB, row 0 carries the LINTEL
7236               	; 	' and row 3 the SILL.
7237               	; 	'
7238               	; 	' THE SILL IS REVEALED AS THE DOORS PART, which falls out of this rather
7239               	; 	' than being arranged: shut, every cell is plain door and there is no
7240               	; 	' sill to see; part-open, only the middle two columns show car and sill;
7241               	; 	' open, all four do. A sill sitting under a shut door would be a ledge
7242               	; 	' with nothing behind it.
7243               	; 	'
7244               	; 	' Nested IFs, never `ccl > 0 AND ccl < 3` -- the 9900 backend miscompiles
7245               	; 	' a compare-AND-compare (CLAUDE.md 3A).
7246               	; car_cell:

8003               cv339
8004               	; 		' THE FIRST STEP OFF THE MARK IS ALWAYS HEARD. sfw is a distance --
8005               	; 		' a step every fifteen pixels -- so a short tap of the stick moved
8006               	; 		' him a few pixels and made NO sound at all. That does not read as
8007               	; 		' a short step, it reads as the controls being ignored, and it is
8008               	; 		' worst exactly where a player taps rather than holds: lining up a
8009               	; 		' jump, or edging around a hazard.
8010               	; 		'
8011               	; 		' Priming the accumulator to the threshold makes the very next pass
8012               	; 		' fire. It does not cheat the RATE: the trigger subtracts fifteen

8942               	;
8943               	; 	' THE VICTROLA, AS CHARACTERS. It never moves, so a sprite spent a
8944               	; 	' scan-line slot on something that can be painted once when the screen is
8945               	; 	' drawn -- and at one 16x16 sprite it could only ever be one colour and
8946               	; 	' one size. Four cells is twice the area for no sprite at all.
8947               	; 	'
8948               	; 	' It stands ON the slab, so it fills the band's rows 2 and 3; row 4 is
8949               	; 	' the floor bar itself -- and a PRIZE uses those same two rows.
8950               	; 	'
8951               	; 	' THEY CAN SHARE A BAND, AND THE CLAIM THAT USED TO BE HERE WAS WRONG.
8952               	; 	' It said the two never share a screen because "genstore keeps prizes off
8953               	; 	' the screens that carry hazards". That stopped being true the moment
8954               	; 	' hazard placement moved into the per-Krook stor_lvl table, and nothing
8955               	; 	' noticed, because the prize table is not part of the level table and
8956               	; 	' every check was written about one object at a time. Two money bags ended
8957               	; 	' up standing on a radio -- not fighting it, since the two routines poke
8958               	; 	' different cells and the later writer simply wins, so they read as one
8959               	; 	' merged object.
8960               	; 	'
8961               	; 	' WHAT KEEPS THEM APART IS COLUMNS. A radio stands at column 7, 15 or 23
8962               	; 	' (see lrc below); genstore's _off_the_rack nudges a prize clear of all
8963               	; 	' three, and checklevels.py reads that arithmetic back out of THIS file
8964               	; 	' and fails the build on any overlap.
8965               	; 	'
8966               	; 	' rdall = 1 paints all four cells, 0 repaints only the top-right one --
8967               	; 	' the pulse. Same address arithmetic either way, so the two cannot drift.
8968               	; 	' A BEAM TOP HANGS OUT OF THE FLOOR ABOVE, and the beam it belongs to has
8969               	; 	' just been taken away. `beam_tops` stamps SLABP -- the floor bar with the
8970               	; 	' support carried up through its lower three pixel rows -- into the slab
8971               	; 	' row above every pillar, and it runs BEFORE the radios and prizes are
8972               	; 	' placed. Clearing a pillar's own cells therefore left three grey pixels
8973               	; 	' dangling from the ceiling with nothing under them.
8974               	; 	'
8975               	; 	' TESTED, NOT ASSUMED: only SLABP is put back to SLAB. The row above the
8976               	; 	' top shopping floor is the ROOF DECK, a different character altogether,
8977               	; 	' and writing a floor bar over it would punch a hole in the roof.
8978               	; 	' A SHELF RUN IS FIVE CELLS WIDE and a radio covers two, so one standing
8979               	; 	' on a counter punched a hole through its middle and left the ends either
8980               	; 	' side -- the same incoherence the dangling pillar had, and worse, because
8981               	; 	' a counter reads as one object. The whole unit goes: walk outward along
8982               	; 	' the band's row 2 while the cell is still a shelf top, clearing it and
8983               	; 	' its bottom half together.
8984               	; 	'
8985               	; 	' Bounded at eight steps. The runs are five, so eight is slack rather
8986               	; 	' than a guess -- and an unbounded walk would run off the end of the row
8987               	; 	' if the name table ever held something unexpected.
8988               	; 	#if NES
8989               	; 	' WHAT THE TEMPLATE PUT IN THIS CELL, for a target that cannot read its
8990               	; 	' own video memory back. #nta is the offset INSIDE the band (0-159) and
8991               	; 	' nbl is the band; the answer is the byte SCREEN blitted there.
8992               	; 	'
8993               	; 	' This is the same arithmetic the blit itself does in draw_band --
8994               	; 	' template id out of stor_ix for (band, screen), times 160, plus the
8995               	; 	' offset -- so the two cannot disagree about what is on screen. It is
8996               	; 	' reading what the cell MEANS, not guessing from where the cell is: a
8997               	; 	' coordinate is a fact about this layout, the character is a fact about
8998               	; 	' the world, and only the second is safe to erase on.
8999               	; 	' SIXTEEN PATTERNS INTO THE BORROWED SLOTS, ONE VBLANK EACH.
9000               	; 	'
9001               	; 	' This is what esc_stand and esc_run cost on this machine. Four sprites is
9002               	; 	' 16 patterns and **a tile here is SIXTEEN bytes** -- two bitplanes -- so
9003               	; 	' the swap is 256 bytes. Three ways to spend that, and only one works:
9004               	; 	'
9005               	; 	'   nes_def         rendering off, ~2 frames of DARK SCREEN every mount.
9006               	; 	'                   This is the flash that was reported for three sessions.
9007               	; 	'   resident art    no upload at all -- but it needs 16 free patterns per
9008               	; 	'                   facing and there are only twelve free in the whole
9009               	; 	'                   table. Tried, and it overwrote Harry's left-facing legs.
9010               	; 	'   queued, chunked <- this. 64 bytes a vblank, four vblanks, picture up
9011               	; 	'                   the whole time.
9012               	; 	'
9013               	; 	' FOUR CHUNKS BECAUSE ONE WILL NOT FIT. The NMI's copy loop runs to the end
9014               	; 	' of its descriptor whatever the raster is doing, and the PPUADDR/PPUSCROLL
9015               	; 	' restore that follows it re-points the PPU mid-frame if it runs late --
9016               	; 	' which is the whole picture jumping for a frame. About 1679 cycles are
9017               	; 	' available after OAM DMA and a copy costs 50 + 14 a byte, so 64 bytes
9018               	; 	' (946) is comfortable and 256 (3634) is not. The WAITs are load-bearing:
9019               	; 	' PPUBUF accumulates for a whole pass, so without them all four descriptors
9020               	; 	' would flush in one vblank and cost exactly what the single call did.
9021               	; 	' checkvblank.py sums the descriptors BETWEEN WAITs for this reason.
9022               	; 	'
9023               	; 	' The cost is four frames at a mount or a dismount, once each, against two
9024               	; 	' frames of black. The caller sets #nsrc; nes_chrinit copies nchr, ncnt,
9025               	; 	' #ncol and nink into zero page rather than consuming the variables, so
9026               	; 	' they only need setting once.
9027               	; 	'
9028               	; 	' THE INTERMEDIATE STATE IS VISIBLE and that is accepted: for a frame or
9029               	; 	' two Harry is part standing and part running. He is stepping onto a
9030               	; 	' staircase at the time, which is exactly when a limb changing shape reads
9031               	; 	' as him changing pose.
9032               	; nes_swp16:
9033               	; 	nchr = P_HSTB
9034               	; 	ntab = 0
9035               	; 	#ncol = 0
9036               	; 	nink = 1
9037               	; 	ncnt = 4
9038               	; 	WAIT
9039               	; 	GOSUB nes_escd
9040               	; 	#nsrc = #nsrc + 32		' four patterns of source art, 8 bytes each
9041               	; 	nchr = nchr + 4
9042               	; 	WAIT
9043               	; 	GOSUB nes_escd
9044               	; 	#nsrc = #nsrc + 32
9045               	; 	nchr = nchr + 4
9046               	; 	WAIT
9047               	; 	GOSUB nes_escd
9048               	; 	#nsrc = #nsrc + 32
9049               	; 	nchr = nchr + 4
9050               	; 	WAIT
9051               	; 	GOSUB nes_escd
9052               	; 	RETURN
9053               	;
9054               	; nes_def:
9055               	; 	' WHAT DEFINE WOULD HAVE DONE. CVBasic implements no DEFINE at all for the
9056               	; 	' NES, on the reading that patterns live in cartridge CHR ROM -- but an
9057               	; 	' iNES header with a CHR-bank count of ZERO asks for 8 KB of CHR-RAM
9058               	; 	' instead, and that is the header CVBasic emits whenever the program uses
9059               	; 	' no BITMAP/CHRROM statement. So the pattern table here is ordinary VRAM
9060               	; 	' and this is the write. assets/nes_chr.asm carries the routine and the
9061               	; 	' reasoning; the caller sets #nsrc, nchr, ncnt and ntab.
9062               	; 	ASM JSR nes_chrup
9063               	; 	RETURN
9064               	;
9065               	; 	' AND THE SAME THING WITHOUT LOSING A FRAME. nes_def turns rendering off
9066               	; 	' and waits for a vblank the NMI therefore never services, so the game's
9067               	; 	' own WAIT then waits for the one after -- about two frames a call. That
9068               	; 	' is free at setup and ruinous anywhere that runs repeatedly. It builds
9069               	; 	' the same bytes into `nesb` and hands the NMI a single copy descriptor
9070               	; 	' instead. See assets/nes_chr.asm.
9071               	; 	'
9072               	; 	' THE NAME IS HISTORICAL: it was written for esc_tick, which redefines six
9073               	; 	' characters EVERY PASS on the two escalator screens and ran visibly slow
9074               	; 	' on nes_def. Nothing about it is escalator-specific -- it takes the same
9075               	; 	' inputs as nes_def plus #nesb, and the title's marquee uses it too, where
9076               	; 	' nes_def was switching the picture off twice a step and reading as a
9077               	; 	' flashing title screen.
9078               	; 	'
9079               	; 	' #nesb must point at a buffer of at least ncnt*16 bytes and is set once
9080               	; 	' in init_tables, which runs before boot: and therefore before the title.
9081               	; nes_escd:
9082               	; 	ASM JSR nes_chrq
9083               	; 	RETURN
9084               	;

9830               	; 	' ONE ACCUMULATOR PER KIND, NOT PER SLOT. Every hazard of a kind moves at
9831               	; 	' that kind's speed, so three calls a pass serve all eight slots.
9832               	; 	'

9834               	; 	' the positive feedback loop CLAUDE.md 3A warns about, where a slow pass is
9835               	; 	' made slower by the very code meant to take the loop rate out of the
9836               	; 	' game's behaviour. It also saves the eight bytes an obacc() would cost,
9837               	; 	' and ColecoVision RAM is the tighter budget.

9871               	; 	' THE BOUNCE PHASE, ON THE SAME CLOCK AS THE JUMP AND AT ITS OLD PERIOD.
9872               	; 	'
9873               	; 	' The jump has always advanced by the frame delta (`kjf = kjf + fdv`) while
9874               	; 	' the bounce advanced once per PASS -- so whether a jump cleared a ball
9875               	; 	' depended on how busy the screen was, and the frame-by-frame property
9876               	; 	' checkball.py proves was exact only at fdv = 1.
9877               	; 	'
9878               	; 	' Stepping the phase by fdv directly would fix the clock and wreck the
9879               	; 	' game: a 32-phase arc would drop from about 1.35 s to 0.55 s, balls
9880               	; 	' bouncing 2.4x faster everywhere. So it gets a fraction of its own --
9881               	; 	' 25/64 of a phase per frame is 23.4 phases a second, against the 23.8 it
9882               	; 	' runs at today. Same bounce, now the same clock as the thing that has to
9883               	; 	' clear it.
9884               	; 	pacc = obac
9885 D58C D820  54 	movb @cvb_OBAC,@cvb_PACC
     D58E 20F4     
     D590 2130     
9886               	; 	psp64 = BOUNCE64
9887 D592 0200  20 	li r0,6400   ; 25*256
     D594 1900

     D598 2138

9890 D59A 06A0  32 	bl @jsr
     D59C A980

     D5A2 2130

10129               	; 	' ONE STEP OF A FRACTIONAL SPEED, FOR WHOEVER IS MOVING.
10130               	; 	'
10131               	; 	' `pacc` in and out, `psp64` in (sixty-fourths of a pixel per FRAME),
10132               	; 	' `pspd` out (whole pixels this pass). CVBasic has no locals, so the caller
10133               	; 	' stages its own accumulator in and takes it back out; that costs four
10134               	; 	' statements against the fourteen this used to be, written out per actor.
10135               	; 	'
10136               	; 	' Harry had the only copy. Kelly, the hazards and the bounce phase all need
10137               	; 	' the same thing -- everything the round clock judges has to advance by
10138               	; 	' ELAPSED FRAMES, or the loop rate becomes a difficulty dial and where the
10139               	; 	' player stands decides the outcome (DESIGN.md 0f-ter).
10140               	; 	'
10141               	; 	' TWO DRAINS CAP THE STEP AT 2 PER FRAME whatever psp64 says (CLAUDE.md
10142               	; 	' 3A: N drains cap the speed at N, and the surplus leaks into a byte that
10143               	; 	' wraps). Every caller is under that: Kelly 102/64 = 1.6, the fastest
10144               	; 	' hazard 76/64 = 1.2, Harry 57/64 = 0.9, the bounce phase 25/64 = 0.4.
10145               	; 	'
10146               	; 	' FIVE FRAMES, AND THREE WAS TOO FEW. At 2 px a frame five frames is 10 px,
10147               	; 	' and to skip a position window an actor must start outside it on one side
10148               	; 	' and land outside on the other, which needs 12. Three was the original bug
10149               	; 	' in miniature: the lift screen runs at almost exactly 20 passes a second,
10150               	; 	' which IS fdv = 3, so every hitch there lost a frame. The clamp exists for
10151               	; 	' a genuine stall and at five it only fires for one.

10231               	; 	'
10232               	; 	' HE RIDES ON THE STEPS rather than beside them -- he used to hold still
10233               	; 	' for the whole flight and then appear at the top, which read as him
10234               	; 	' teleporting up a floor. Same fixed 2-across-per-1-up PER PASS as the
10235               	; 	' player, clocked by the animation for the same reason (see move_kelly):
10236               	; 	' a rider and the cyclic animation he stands on must share one clock, and
10237               	; 	' that clock cannot be the frame delta.
10238               	; 	'

10240               	; 	' you up, so the flight whose TOP lands on this floor is a one-way exit
10241               	; 	' belonging to the crook alone: he steps on at the head and rides it the
10242               	; 	' wrong way.
10243               	; 	'

10245               	; 	' identical variables, differing only in the sign of the horizontal step
10246               	; 	' and the direction of the level change -- which is what "the same
10247               	; 	' staircase from the other end" means arithmetically. `romclones.py` could

10640               	; 	' THE SIXTEENTH-PIXEL ACCUMULATOR. hx is one unsigned byte per screen
10641               	; 	' (2), so there is nowhere to keep a fraction -- the fraction lives here
10642               	; 	' and is spent as whole pixels. THREE IFs, not a loop and not a divide:
10643               	; 	' `%` and `/` both compile to a real TMS9900 DIV (CLAUDE.md 3A) and this
10644               	; 	' runs every pass.
10645               	; 	'
10646               	; 	' THE NUMBER OF DRAINS IS A CEILING ON THE SPEED, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE
10647               	; 	' POINT OF THIS COMMENT. Each IF can spend one whole pixel, so N drains
10648               	; 	' cap hspd at N px per pass NO MATTER WHAT hsp64 SAYS. The invariant is:
10649               	; 	'
10650               	; 	'     hacc is under 16 on entry, and hsp64 is at most 48,
10651               	; 	'     so hacc is under 64 here and three drains always suffice.
10652               	; 	'
10653               	; 	' KEEP hsp64 <= 48. This was quarter-pixels with TWO drains and the same
10654               	; 	' invariant written the same way -- "hsp4 is at most 8, so it can never
10655               	; 	' need a third" -- and it was correct until somebody set hsp4 = 9 without
10656               	; 	' re-reading it. The crook then ran at a flat 2.0 px/pass while every
10657               	; 	' comment, the design table and assets/checkchase.py all said 2.25, and
10658               	; 	' the surplus quarter leaked into hacc and wrapped the byte every 256
10659               	; 	' passes. Nothing failed; he simply arrived two thirds of a screen short
10660               	; 	' of his own escape. checkchase.py now counts these IFs and refuses a
10661               	; 	' speed the drains cannot deliver.
10662               	; 	'
10663               	; 	' 7, NOT 6, AND THE REASON IS MEASURED. Tracked off the reference video
10664               	; 	' (DESIGN.md 4a), the 2600's Kelly covers 0.40 screen widths a second and
10665               	; 	' its Harry 0.193 -- a ratio of 2.07. At hsp4 = 6 ours was 2.67, and the
10666               	; 	' crook visibly strolled. 7 brings it to 2.29. 8 would match the original
10667               	; 	' exactly and cannot be used: Kelly's route here is 1.95x Harry's, so a
10668               	; 	' speed ratio of 2.0 leaves the on-foot chase 0.2 s of slack, which is no
10669               	; 	' chase at all. checkchase.py holds the line.
10670               	; 	' STILL RUNNING FROM THE STAIRS -- and this has to come BEFORE the move,
10671               	; 	' not after it. It sat below the two `IF hmv` blocks, where all it could
10672               	; 	' still reach was the animation counter: he faced the right way, played
10673               	; 	' the run cycle and did not travel a pixel. He stood at the foot of the
10674               	; 	' flight looking busy.
10675               	; 	'
10676               	; 	' TWO THINGS END THE RUN, AND BOTH ARE VISIBLE ON SCREEN.
10677               	; 	'
10678               	; 	' THE KOP ARRIVING ON THIS FLOOR OUTRANKS IT. This used to override the
10679               	; 	' flee as well as the climb, so for the whole of the run he held one
10680               	; 	' heading no matter where Kelly was -- and ran straight into him without
10681               	; 	' appearing to notice he was there. The flee above has already worked out
10682               	; 	' which way is away; clearing the run simply lets it stand.
10683               	; 	'
10684               	; 	' AND REACHING THE END WALL ENDS IT. It used to be a count of passes,

10771               	; 	' HE WALKS BY REAL TIME, NOT BY LOOP PASS -- one accumulate-and-drain per
10772               	; 	' ELAPSED FRAME rather than per pass. Everything that moves here used to be
10773               	; 	' per pass while the CLOCK is paced by the frame delta, so a busy screen
10774               	; 	' slowed Harry in real seconds and the clock did not slow with him: the
10775               	; 	' same uninterrupted escape finished with nine timer units in hand from a
10776               	; 	' light screen and none at all from the lift screen, decided by where the
10777               	; 	' player happened to be standing. Now he covers the same ground per second
10778               	; 	' wherever anybody is (DESIGN.md 0f-ter).
10779               	; 	'
10780               	; 	' A LOOP, NOT A MULTIPLY. `*` compiles to a real TMS9900 MPY, and reading a
10781               	; 	' 16-bit variable straight after one returns the product's HIGH word
10782               	; 	' (CLAUDE.md 3A). fdv is 1..3 here, so this is at most three adds.
10783               	; 	'
10784               	; 	' SIXTY-FOURTHS, AND ONLY TWO DRAINS -- both fall out of accumulating per
10785               	; 	' FRAME instead of per pass. He covers under a pixel a frame, so two drains
10786               	; 	' are ample where the per-pass version needed three; and the finer unit is
10787               	; 	' what makes the speed tunable at all. In sixteenths one step was about six
10788               	; 	' SECONDS of his route, so nothing landed near the buzzer; in sixty-fourths
10789               	; 	' it is about one and a half. Keep hsp64 <= 128: hacc is under 64 on entry,
10790               	; 	' so 64 + 128 stays inside a byte and two drains always suffice.
10791               	; 	'
10792               	; 	' AND THE STEP IS CLAMPED TO THREE FRAMES' WORTH, WHICH IS NOT A DETAIL.
10793               	; 	' Two tests sample his position once a pass and neither interpolates:
10794               	; 	'
10795               	; 	'   ARRIVAL   `hdx < 6` around the escalator or the roof door -- an ELEVEN
10796               	; 	'             pixel window. A step over 10 px can jump clean across it and
10797               	; 	'             he never arrives at all.
10798               	; 	'   THE CATCH `hdd < CATCHR` is 12, a 23-wide band, and Kelly closes 4 of
10799               	; 	'             it himself -- so Harry over ~18 px could pass through the Kop
10800               	; 	'             between two passes without either sample being inside it.
10801               	; 	'
10802               	; 	' The clamp and the drains live in pace_step now, with the reasoning; the
10803               	; 	' numbers above are what sized them. Measured: TIME 02 on the lift screen
10804               	; 	' against TIME 04 on a light one when the clamp was 3, and 00 against 09
10805               	; 	' before any of this.
10806               	; 	'
10807               	; 	' The ESCALATOR RIDE is deliberately untouched: it returns above this,
10808               	; 	' clocked one step per pass to stay locked to the moving staircase. A rider
10809               	; 	' advanced by the frame delta either drifts off the treads or makes the
10810               	; 	' steps run backwards (CLAUDE.md 3A, DESIGN.md 0f). It is about 3% of his
10811               	; 	' journey.
10812               	; 	'
10813               	; 	' `hanim` still advances by hspd and is still an ODOMETER -- pixels
10814               	; 	' travelled, not time -- so the run cycle stays locked to the ground at any
10815               	; 	' rate. A 9 px step moves it exactly one pose of its 8 px beat.

11276               	;
11277               	; 	' ======================================================================
11278               	; 	' COLLISIONS -- pure arithmetic against RAM, no VDP reads
11279               	; 	' ======================================================================
11280               	; 	' Kelly's box is [kfh, kfh + kh) above the slab; an obstacle's is
11281               	; 	' [ohb, oht). The ball's inset hitbox is what makes 8..10 avoidable both
11282               	; 	' ways -- without it there is a height at which the ball can be neither
11283               	; 	' jumped nor ducked, and an unavoidable hazard is not difficulty.
11284               	; 	' ONE HIT PER CONTACT, WITH A REFRACTORY PERIOD.
11285               	; 	'
11286               	; 	' The overlap test is true on every frame the player is touching
11287               	; 	' something, so with no latch at all one clumsy cart charges nine seconds
11288               	; 	' several times over -- and what the player sees is the clock jumping by
11289               	; 	' 27, from which the only available conclusion is that the penalty is
11290               	; 	' broken.
11291               	; 	'
11292               	; 	' A latch that clears on the first non-overlapping frame is still not
11293               	; 	' enough, and the case that breaks it is the BOUNCING BALL: it rises off
11294               	; 	' the player between bounces, which is a genuine loss of contact, so a
11295               	; 	' player standing still under one is taxed on every single bounce while
11296               	; 	' being given no opportunity to do anything about it. Technically two
11297               	; 	' collisions; in play, one situation.
11298               	; 	'
11299               	; 	' So obht() is a countdown, not a flag. A hit sets it to HITREF; it ticks
11300               	; 	' down only while the player is CLEAR, and the same obstacle cannot charge
11301               	; 	' again until it reaches zero. Contact holds the count up, so parking
11302               	; 	' inside something never earns a second penalty either.
11303               	; coll_obst:
11304               cvb_COLL_OBST

11670               	; 	' THE FLOOR CLEARS WHEN YOU ARE HIT, and stays clear until you re-enter
11671               	; 	' the screen. Nine seconds is a heavy penalty on a fifty-unit clock, and
11672               	; 	' taking it while still standing among the things that charged it -- with
11673               	; 	' a second hazard 48 px behind the first -- is how one mistake becomes
11674               	; 	' three. Clearing the row makes the penalty a single event you can walk
11675               	; 	' away from.
11676               	; 	'
11677               	; 	' BOTH SLOTS, WHATEVER IS IN THEM. Radios used to be exempt: they are
11678               	; 	' CHARACTERS stamped into the name table rather than sprites, so zeroing
11679               	; 	' the kind would have stopped them colliding while leaving them plainly
11680               	; 	' visible on the shelf, and a fixture that is still there has to still be
11681               	; 	' there. That was a reason to UNDRAW them, not a reason to keep them --
11682               	; 	' and it left the one hazard that cannot leave on its own as the only one
11683               	; 	' the mercy did not cover. haz_off now takes the characters with it.
11684               	; 	'
11685               	; 	' NOTHING RESTORES IT HERE. load_band repopulates the band from the
11686               	; 	' template, and it runs only on a seam crossing or a round start, so
11687               	; 	' "until the screen is re-entered" costs no state and no timer: leave and
11688               	; 	' come back and the hazards are simply placed again.
11689               	; 	'
11690               	; 	' THE CALL ITSELF IS IN THE MAIN LOOP, at the end of the freeze -- see
11691               	; 	' the hfz block there for why.
11692               	; 	' A HIT DOES NOT END A JUMP. This used to force ST_RUN and zero the arc,
11693               	; 	' which dropped him straight down out of mid-air onto whatever he happened
11694               	; 	' to be over -- and since the arc is ballistic and ignores the stick once
11695               	; 	' he is airborne (0l), that read as the game taking the controls away
11696               	; 	' rather than as a hit landing. The penalty is the nine units and the
11697               	; 	' knock flash; where he comes down is still his own arc.
11698               	; 	'

11859               	; 	' AND THEY HAVE TO BE AT THE SAME HEIGHT, NOT MERELY ON THE SAME FLOOR.
11860               	; 	'
11861               	; 	' `hlv` does not change until a ride ENDS -- a crook stepping onto a
11862               	; 	' flight keeps the floor he left until he arrives at the next one. So
11863               	; 	' while he was most of a storey up or down the stairs he still counted as
11864               	; 	' standing on the floor he started from, and a Kop who ran over the head
11865               	; 	' of the flight arrested him through the floor. Reported from play:
11866               	; 	' "I run over top of him, even though we do not touch".
11867               	; 	'
11868               	; 	' It is the same shape of bug as the catch that fired at MAXIMUM
11869               	; 	' separation: a test that is right about one axis and silent about the
11870               	; 	' other, where the silent one happens to be true nearly all the time.
11871               	; 	'

11874               	; 	' So both are collected as POSITIVE heights on opposite sides -- Kelly's
11875               	; 	' climb plus Harry's descent on one side, Harry's climb on the other --
11876               	; 	' and the difference is taken between two numbers that cannot go
11877               	; 	' negative. Two riders passing on the same flight measure the sum of

12043               	; 	' KELLY'S HAT DOES NOT FLASH WHEN HE IS HIT. It used to alternate to white

12046               	; 	' That argument no longer holds: the knockback still throws him, the HUD's
12047               	; 	' digits still drop by nine, and the hit now has a sound that is allowed to
12048               	; 	' finish. Three signals for one event, and the flash was the least legible
12049               	; 	' of them -- a two-frame colour swap on a 16 px hat, during the one moment
12050               	; 	' the player is looking at where they are being pushed.
12051               	; 	'
12052               	; 	' Dropping it retires `kcol` with it: the hat is C_KHAT always, so the
12053               	; 	' colour goes straight into the SPRITE calls below and the per-pass
12054               	; 	' variable, its assignment and two nested IFs all go.

12056               	; 	' `knock` STAYS. It is the knockback, which is the part that is felt.
12057               	; 	' KELLY IS SPRITES 0, 1 AND 2 and nothing else ever is -- the VDP drops
12058               	; 	' the highest-numbered sprites on an over-full scanline, so the lowest
12059               	; 	' slots are the ones that can never disappear, and the player is the one
12060               	; 	' thing that must never disappear.
12061               	; 	'
12062               	; 	' THE BAND SPRITES SHARE A y ON PURPOSE. Slots 0 and 1 both sit at ky and
12063               	; 	' between them cover rows 0-15; slot 2 sits at ky+16. Boxes 0/1 and box 2
12064               	; 	' never share a scanline, so an actor costs at most TWO boxes on any line
12065               	; 	' -- and the VDP counts boxes, not pixels, so an empty overlap would have
12066               	; 	' cost just as much as a full one. Two actors meeting is four, exactly
12067               	; 	' the per-line limit, which is why obstacles are suppressed on Harry's
12068               	; 	' floor rather than merely being a kindness.

13047               	;
13048               	; 	' ======================================================================
13049               	; 	' THE SCANNER
13050               	; 	' ======================================================================
13051               	; 	' Rows 21-23, 16 chars wide, centred: 48 characters whose PATTERNS are
13052               	; 	' poked directly, so a moving dot costs two writes and no name-table
13053               	; 	' traffic. With the flip (DESIGN.md 2a) this is how you know where Harry
13054               	; 	' is at all -- he can be one pixel off-screen and completely invisible.
13055               	; 	'
13056               	; 	' Rows 21-23 all sit in the THIRD screen third, so every scanner pattern
13057               	; 	' is at base 4096 and no third-selection arithmetic is needed.
13058               	; 	'
13059               	; 	' BOTH DOTS ARE WHITE and Kelly's BLINKS. The manual wants Kelly black
13060               	; 	' and Harry white, but this is the TMS9918's two-colours-per-8x1-cell
13061               	; 	' mode: a black dot and a white dot on the same pixel row of the same
13062               	; 	' character cannot both exist. Blinking distinguishes them with one
13063               	; 	' colour, which is what RallyX does with its player dot.
13064               	; 	' THE STEPS MOVE, AND EVERY ESCALATOR ON SCREEN MOVES WITH THEM. A flight
13065               	; 	' is twelve characters -- six per direction, sliced out of a rendered
13066               	; 	' 64x40 bitmap by genart.py -- so rewriting those twelve PATTERNS animates
13067               	; 	' the lot: 96 bytes, no name-table traffic, and the same cost whether one
13068               	; 	' flight is visible or ten. The phases slide the cells ALONG the slope, so
13069               	; 	' the steps travel up the flight rather than drifting sideways.
13070               	; esc_tick:
13071               cvb_ESC_TICK
13072               	; 	' ONLY SCREENS 0 AND 7 CARRY A FLIGHT, so six screens in eight skip this
13073               	; 	' entirely -- which is what makes rewriting the cells every frame
13074               	; 	' affordable. Nested, not `klsc > 0 AND klsc < 7`: the 9900 backend
13075               	; 	' miscompiles a compare-AND-compare (CLAUDE.md 3A).
13076               	; 	IF klsc > 0 THEN
13077 EBB6 D020  34 	movb @cvb_KLSC,r0
     EBB8 21AC     
13078 EBBA 0201  20 	li r1,256   ; 1*256
     EBBC 0100     
13079 EBBE 9040  18 	cb r0,r1
13080 EBC0 1402  14 	jhe cv803
13081 EBC2 0460  28 	b @cv802
     EBC4 EBDA

13094               cv802
13095               	; 	' ONE PHASE PER PASS, AND NEVER MORE. There are four phases covering an
13096               	; 	' 8 px period, so advancing by the frame delta ALIASES: at fdv 2 the
13097               	; 	' pattern flips between two positions half a period apart and the
13098               	; 	' direction stops being readable, and at fdv 3 the sequence runs 0,3,2,1
13099               	; 	' -- the staircase visibly runs BACKWARDS, carrying its steps down while
13100               	; 	' the rider goes up. That is the wagon-wheel effect, and no amount of
13101               	; 	' phase arithmetic fixes it: a 4-phase cycle can only be stepped by 1.
13102               	; 	'
13103               	; 	' So the ANIMATION is the clock here, and the rider is paced from it --
13104               	; 	' see move_kelly, which advances him by the same fixed 2-and-1 per pass
13105               	; 	' rather than by fdv. Locking the two together is the only way they
13106               	; 	' cannot drift, and it is what "the player moves at the rate the steps
13107               	; 	' carry him" actually means. The cost is that a ride takes 36 passes
13108               	; 	' rather than 36 frames, so it slows down when the loop does -- which is
13109               	; 	' the honest behaviour for a machine that is carrying you.
13110               	; 	escp = escp + 1
13111 EBDA D020  34 	movb @cvb_ESCP,r0
     EBDC 20B5

     EBF6 20B5     
13122               cv806
13123               	; 	#if NES
13124               	; 	' A VBLANK OF ITS OWN, AND THIS IS THE WHOLE-SCREEN FLASH.
13125               	; 	'
13126               	; 	' PPUBUF is not flushed when it is written -- it ACCUMULATES for the whole
13127               	; 	' pass and the NMI empties it in one go, so every VPOKE the radar makes,
13128               	; 	' every HUD digit and this upload all land in the SAME vblank. And the
13129               	; 	' handler's copy loop does not stop when vblank ends: it runs to the end of
13130               	; 	' the descriptor and then writes PPUADDR and both PPUSCROLLs, which
13131               	; 	' mid-frame re-points the PPU's own render address. The rest of that frame
13132               	; 	' is drawn from the wrong place. On screen that is not a dropped tile, it
13133               	; 	' is the ENTIRE PICTURE jumping for a frame -- which is what has been
13134               	; 	' reported, repeatedly, as the screen flashing on an escalator.
13135               	; 	'
13136               	; 	' The arithmetic says it cannot be anything else. NTSC vblank is about
13137               	; 	' 2273 CPU cycles; NMI entry, the flicker test and OAM DMA spend ~560 of
13138               	; 	' them before a single byte is copied. A copy descriptor costs ~50 cycles
13139               	; 	' plus 14 a byte, so these six characters -- 96 bytes, because a tile is
13140               	; 	' SIXTEEN bytes in two bitplanes, not eight -- are ~1400 on their own.
13141               	; 	' That leaves about 270 cycles, or SIX single-byte pokes, for everything
13142               	; 	' else the pass queued. The radar alone beats that whenever a dot moves.
13143               	; 	'
13144               	; 	' Nothing smaller fixes it, because the overrun is per FRAME, not per
13145               	; 	' second: slowing the animation down just makes the bad frames rarer.
13146               	; 	' Splitting the six characters across two frames tears the staircase, and
13147               	; 	' only three of the six have a constant second bitplane, so dropping a
13148               	; 	' plane does not buy a frame's worth either. What DOES work is giving the
13149               	; 	' upload a vblank with nothing else in it: this WAIT flushes the pass's
13150               	; 	' radar and HUD writes, and the descriptor queued below is then almost all
13151               	; 	' the next vblank has to carry -- ~1960 cycles of 2273, inside the window
13152               	; 	' with room to spare.
13153               	; 	'
13154               	; 	' IT COSTS ONE FRAME A PASS, on the two screens that carry a flight and
13155               	; 	' nowhere else -- esc_tick has already returned on the other six. The
13156               	; 	' rider is paced from the animation rather than from the frame delta (see
13157               	; 	' below), so a slower pass slows the ride too and the two cannot drift.
13158               	; 	WAIT
13159               	; 	#endif
13160               	; 	' ONLY THE CELLS THAT MOVE, AND ONLY THIS SCREEN'S. genart.py measures
13161               	; 	' which cells move -- the step cells and the COMPOSITE copies of them
13162               	; 	' that cross a floor -- and groups them WEST then EAST, because only one
13163               	; 	' direction is ever on screen: screen 0 carries a west flight and screen
13164               	; 	' 7 an east one.
13165               	; 	'
13166               	; 	' THIS IS THE ONLY PER-PASS WORK UNIQUE TO THESE TWO SCREENS, and it is
13167               	; 	' `define_char`, which in bitmap mode is LDIRVM3 -- the TRIPLE copy, once
13168               	; 	' per screen third. It therefore costs three times what the character
13169               	; 	' count suggests, which is why these screens run slower than the rest.
13170               	; 	'
13171               	; 	' THE WEST SCREEN USED TO COST HALF AS MUCH AGAIN, because it carries TWO
13172               	; 	' flights: floor 1's crosses into a shop floor and floor 3's into the
13173               	; 	' roof, so it needed both composite sets -- nine characters against the
13174               	; 	' east's six, 216 bytes a pass against 144. It measured 20 passes a
13175               	; 	' second where the east screen managed 24-26. The two sets are
13176               	; 	' PIXEL-IDENTICAL and are never wanted in the same screen THIRD, so they
13177               	; 	' share their characters now and are told apart by the per-third colour
13178               	; 	' table (see esc_deck_col in setup). Six either side.
13179               	; 	'
13180               	; 	' The handrail and the frame sit past the end of both ranges and never
13181               	; 	' move at all.
13182               	; 	IF klsc = 0 THEN
13183 EBF8 D020  34 	movb @cvb_KLSC,r0
     EBFA 21AC

13479               	; 	' ------------------------------------------------- the scanner's furniture
13480               	; 	' Without this the scanner is two dots in a void: you can see THAT Harry is
13481               	; 	' somewhere, but not what he is near, which is the one thing you actually
13482               	; 	' need when he is off-screen. Floor lines say which level, the slashes say
13483               	; 	' where that floor's escalator is, and the bar says where the elevator is --
13484               	; 	' exactly the three things the manual lists.

13791               	; 	' 0 set everywhere, see scan_wipe -- and black is index 0, so the flight
13792               	; 	' is made by taking plane 0 bits OUT. Same pixels, opposite sense.

13897               	; 	' Blank the canvas by WRITING zeros rather than copying 384 of them out
13898               	; 	' of ROM. This runs twice a game -- at setup and on a new Krook -- so a
13899               	; 	' loop costs nothing anybody can perceive, and it hands the fixed area
13900               	; 	' back the best part of half a kilobyte, which is the budget that
13901               	; 	' actually binds. Paced in bursts: a few hundred VDP writes in a single
13902               	; 	' frame are silently dropped (CLAUDE.md 3A).

13905               	; 	' THIS ADDRESS IS A CHARACTER CODE IN DISGUISE, AND IT WENT STALE.
13906               	; 	' 4096 is the pattern table's BOTTOM THIRD -- rows 16-23, which is
13907               	; 	' band 0 and the radar together -- and the canvas characters begin at
13908               	; 	' genart's SCAN_FIRST, so the base is 4096 + SCAN_FIRST*8. It was
13909               	; 	' written out by hand as 4096 + 160*8 when SCAN_FIRST was 160; art
13910               	; 	' added later moved SCAN_FIRST to 208 and nothing moved this with it,
13911               	; 	' so the wipe zeroed the 48 characters BELOW the canvas and never
13912               	; 	' touched the canvas at all.
13913               	; 	'
13914               	; 	' Two of those forty-eight are STRUCTURE. ENDWALL is the building's
13915               	; 	' outside wall and SLABP is a pillar's cap. Blanking a pattern in ONE
13916               	; 	' THIRD leaves a character that draws correctly everywhere else and
13917               	; 	' falls back to its own background colour here -- so the GROUND FLOOR's
13918               	; 	' outside wall turned into plain green while the identical wall one
13919               	; 	' storey up was perfect, and the ground floor's pillars lost the brick
13920               	; 	' carried up through the bar above them. ENDWALL appears only on
13921               	; 	' screens 0 and 7, which is exactly why it was reported as happening
13922               	; 	' only on the escalator screens, mirrored side to side.
13923               	; 	'
13924               	; 	' The name table was correct the whole time. Probing it said so, four
13925               	; 	' times. It was the GLYPH that was empty, in one third only -- which a
13926               	; 	' probe that copies the character somewhere else to look at it cannot
13927               	; 	' see, because the copy renders from a different third's pattern.
13928               	; 	'
13929               	; 	' renumber.py rewrites this line from genart.SCAN_FIRST, and
13930               	; 	' checkstruct.py fails the build if the two disagree.

13955               	; 	' by the same offset the PPU address uses, so it grows with the stride --
13956               	; 	' half of what it holds is the second bitplane, which this port never sets
13957               	; 	' and scan_or1 therefore never reads as ink.
13958               	; 	' AND THE CANVAS IS WIPED TO GREEN, NOT TO BLACK.
13959               	; 	'
13960               	; 	' On the TI a blank canvas is zeros and the COLOUR TABLE says what the
13961               	; 	' background is. There is no colour table here: a pixel's colour is its
13962               	; 	' two bitplane bits, so "green background" means plane 0 SET everywhere
13963               	; 	' and plane 1 clear -- index 1, which is the store's green in P0.
13964               	; 	'
13965               	; 	' THAT INVERTS THE SENSE OF EVERY FEATURE DRAWN ON TOP. The floor lines
13966               	; 	' add plane 1 to reach index 3 (gold), and the escalator diagonals CLEAR
13967               	; 	' plane 0 to reach index 0 (the backdrop, black) -- see scan_or1, which
13968               	; 	' is why it ANDs here and ORs on the TI. Writing zeros here instead would
13969               	; 	' leave the instrument black-on-black and the flights invisible.
13970               	; 	'
13971               	; 	' A tile is sixteen bytes: 0-7 are plane 0 and 8-15 plane 1, so the byte's
13972               	; 	' position within its tile decides which it is.
13973               	; 	' AND THE MARGINS ARE GREY, WHICH IS THE OTHER BITPLANE PAIR.
13974               	; 	'
13975               	; 	' The canvas is three character rows -- 24 pixel rows -- of which the
13976               	; 	' instrument uses the middle SIXTEEN (rows 4-19: four levels of four).
13977               	; 	' The outer eight are deliberate air, four above and four below, so the
13978               	; 	' radar does not butt against the shop floor above it or the screen edge
13979               	; 	' below. On the TI those rows take the scanner's own background; here they
13980               	; 	' are index 2, the store's grey, against the instrument's green.
13981               	; 	'

13983               	; 	' has to change: index 1 green is plane 0, index 2 grey is plane 1, and
13984               	; 	' the floor lines and flights work on top of those (scan_furn, scan_or1).
13985               	; 	'

14513               	;
14514               	; #if NES
14515               	; 	' ----------------------------------------------------------------------
14516               	; 	' THE ATTRIBUTE TABLE -- the NES's only way of giving two parts of the
14517               	; 	' screen different colours.
14518               	; 	'
14519               	; 	' 64 bytes at $23C0. Each byte covers FOUR character rows and four
14520               	; 	' columns, split into four 2x2 quadrants of two bits each: bits 0-1 top
14521               	; 	' left, 2-3 top right, 4-5 bottom left, 6-7 bottom right.
14522               	; 	'
14523               	; 	' The picture sits three rows down for overscan, which lands the regions
14524               	; 	' on block boundaries almost by luck:
14525               	; 	'
14526               	; 	'   byte row 0   name rows 0-3    the HUD is row 3  -> bottom quads P1
14527               	; 	'   byte row 1   name rows 4-7    the sky, top half -> P2, bottom -> P3
14528               	; 	'   byte rows 2+ name rows 8-29   the store         -> P0
14529               	; 	'
14530               	; 	' $50 is "bottom two quadrants on palette 1"; $FA is "top two on palette
14531               	; 	' 2, bottom two on palette 3", which is what splits the sunset into a
14532               	; 	' blue band over a warm one. Written as bare literals because this is the
14533               	; 	' one place the bit layout is visible, and naming them would hide it.
14534               	; 	'
14535               	; 	' 64 VPOKEs is 192 bytes of PPU queue, and WRTVRM waits when the 64-byte
14536               	; 	' buffer fills, so this paces itself across three frames and cannot
14537               	; 	' overrun vblank the way a single big SCREEN blit can.
14538               	; nes_attr:
14539               	; 	#nav = 9152			' $23C0
14540               	; 	FOR nai = 0 TO 7
14541               	; 		VPOKE #nav,80
14542               	; 		#nav = #nav + 1
14543               	; 	NEXT nai
14544               	; 	FOR nai = 0 TO 7
14545               	; 		VPOKE #nav,170			' $AA -- the whole sky band on P2, no second palette
14546               	; 		#nav = #nav + 1
14547               	; 	NEXT nai
14548               	; 	FOR nai = 0 TO 47
14549               	; 		VPOKE #nav,0
14550               	; 		#nav = #nav + 1
14551               	; 	NEXT nai
14552               	; 	RETURN
14553               	; #endif
14554               	;

14556               	; 	' DIV on this CPU, and only run when the value actually changes.

14999               	;
15000               	; 	' THE BONUS IS COUNTED OUT, NOT AWARDED. Dropping the whole sum into the
15001               	; 	' score in one frame tells the player a number; ticking the clock down a
15002               	; 	' unit at a time, with the score climbing and a beat under each step,
15003               	; 	' tells them what the number was FOR. It is the pay-off for every second
15004               	; 	' they saved, and every arcade game of this era spends a moment on it.
15005               	; 	'
15006               	; 	' It also costs nothing to get right: the loop already has to run down
15007               	; 	' `tsec`, so the animation IS the calculation, and the repeated-addition
15008               	; 	' note below stops applying -- each step adds one band's worth.
15009               	; 	'
15010               	; 	' x100 for Krooks 1-9, x200 for 10-15, x300 from 16. Two independent
15011               	; 	' sources agree on those bands; the manual's own wording suggests
15012               	; 	' 1-8 / 9-16 / 17+ and DESIGN.md 0 records the disagreement.
15013               	; 	'
15014               	; 	' IN UNITS OF TEN, WHICH IS WHAT THE SCORE IS COUNTED IN, so the bands are
15015               	; 	' 10 / 20 / 30 and not 100 / 200 / 300.
15016               	; 	'
15017               	; 	' They were 100 / 200 / 300 and paid TEN TIMES the right bonus -- 1,000 a
15018               	; 	' time unit where the original pays 100. `add_score` takes `#addv` in units
15019               	; 	' of ten (the prize beside it is `#addv = 5` for fifty points, and the bonus
15020               	; 	' Kop threshold is `#nextk = 1000` for ten thousand), so writing the band in
15021               	; 	' POINTS here shifted every tally one decimal place. Reported from play as
15022               	; 	' "it seems like you awarded 1000 per time unit left" -- exactly right.
15023               	; 	'
15024               	; 	' Nothing failed: 1,000 a unit is a plausible-looking number, the digits
15025               	; 	' all line up, and the only symptom is a score that runs away. The tell is
15026               	; 	' a constant written in a different unit from the routine it is passed to,
15027               	; 	' which is the same class of fault as the px-per-pass speeds in 3A.
15028               	; 	'
15029               	; 	' (This is also why the old comment here said "#bval MUST BE 16-BIT: 300
15030               	; 	' does not fit in a byte". At 10 / 20 / 30 it would, but it stays 16-bit
15031               	; 	' because `#addv` is, and a byte here would buy two bytes of ROM in
15032               	; 	' exchange for a truncation trap the next time somebody edits a band.)
15033               	; bonus_count:
15034               cvb_BONUS_COUNT
15035               	; 	' THE CLOCK IS ABOUT TO BE COUNTED DOWN, so the field has to be up --

15149               	;
15150               	; 	' AND IT ENDS ON ITS LAST BLIP -- there is no closing accent.
15151               	; 	'
15152               	; 	' Two were tried. The bench's own ending for this variant rose a fourth,
15153               	; 	' to 2,542 Hz, and a square wave there is a shriek -- the same fault the
15154               	; 	' pickup was rewritten for. Dropping it an OCTAVE BELOW the ticks, to
15155               	; 	' 518 Hz, was reported the same way, and that one cannot be too high by
15156               	; 	' any measure: it is the lowest note in the effect.
15157               	; 	'
15158               	; 	' So the complaint is not the pitch, it is the extra note. A tally is
15159               	; 	' arithmetic, and arithmetic finishes when the last term is added; a
15160               	; 	' flourish after it is a second event the player has to interpret, and
15161               	; 	' the HUD has already said the clock is empty. The count stops when the
15162               	; 	' counting stops.
15163               	;
15164               	; 	' `calc_bonus` USED TO LIVE HERE and computed the whole sum by repeated
15165               	; 	' addition, to dodge two hazards at once: `tsec * bmul` is an 8-bit
15166               	; 	' product (a 50-unit capture in the x300 band pays 15,000, six times past
15167               	; 	' a byte), and multiplying properly lands on the MPY/r0 hazard where a
15168               	; 	' 16-bit variable read straight after being multiplied returns the
15169               	; 	' product's high word. Counting the bonus out a unit at a time (above)
15170               	; 	' removes the multiply entirely rather than working around it -- the loop
15171               	; 	' the player watches IS the arithmetic.
15172               	; 	'
15173               	; 	' It also fixed the last-tick case for free: `bn_loop` tests `tsec = 0`
15174               	; 	' on entry, where the old `FOR bi = 1 TO tsec` would have run its body
15175               	; 	' once and paid a full multiplier for no time at all (CLAUDE.md 3A).
15176               	;

15224               	; 	' store. The hit that ENDS a round is the worst case: `do_hit` sets tout
15225               	; 	' before the freeze starts and the main loop leaves on the very next pass,

15229               	; 	' the picture that caused it. Nothing is moving -- the pause ticks sfx_tick

15345               	; 	' Silence every channel FIRST. SOUND latches, and the per-channel decay

15348               	; 	' CVBasic sticky-audio failure.

15475               	;
15476               	; 	' A SOUND STILL PLAYING WHEN THE ROUND ENDS IS ALLOWED TO FINISH.
15477               	; 	'
15478               	; 	' This used to open with a bare `GOSUB snd_off`, which cut it dead. That
15479               	; 	' was not an accident: the decay counters are ticked by the MAIN LOOP, and
15480               	; 	' this pause REPLACES the main loop, so a tone left latched with nothing
15481               	; 	' ticking it hangs for the full ninety frames -- the sticky-audio failure
15482               	; 	' this game has already shipped twice. The answer is to DRAIN the counters
15483               	; 	' rather than to stop silencing.
15484               	; 	'
15485               	; 	' CLEAR THE PENDING LATCHES FIRST. sf* flags are sounds that have not
15486               	; 	' happened yet; left set, the drain below would START one and the pause
15487               	; 	' would end with a fresh note ringing into the next round.
15488               	; 	'
15489               	; 	' THEN TICK sfx_tick WHOLE, not some decay-only part of it. The five
15490               	; 	' counters do not all live in one place: sot, sht and spt are a block at
15491               	; 	' the tail, but spz (the prize arpeggio) and swt (the jump warble) tick up
15492               	; 	' among the code that starts sounds. Draining only the tail would finish a
15493               	; 	' footstep and still cut the arpeggio, which is the one effect with a
15494               	; 	' phrase worth saving. Calling the whole routine also leaves the write
15495               	; 	' order on CHANNEL 2 alone, which spz and spt share.
15496               	; 	'
15497               	; 	' EVERY THIRD FRAME, because the main loop runs about 2.5 frames per pass
15498               	; 	' and this loop waits one frame per turn. Ticking every frame would play
15499               	; 	' everything at two and a half times its tuned speed. Three frames a tick
15500               	; 	' is ~17% slow and gives 30 ticks against the longest effect's 20 passes.
15501               	; 	'
15502               	; 	' THE LOOP COUNTS TICKS, NOT FRAMES, which is what makes the pacing free.
15503               	; 	' Counting 91 frames and firing on every third needs a second counter, an
15504               	; 	' increment and a test -- 48 bytes, on a fixed area with 66 left. Counting
15505               	; 	' 31 TICKS of three WAITs each is the same 93 frames and the same three
15506               	; 	' frames per tick, with none of that. The duration changes by two frames.
15507               	; 	'
15508               	; 	' snd_off still runs at the END, as the backstop for anything the drain
15509               	; 	' did not finish.
15510               	; pause_beat:
15511               cvb_PAUSE_BEAT

     F99A A980
