15873               	;
15874               	; 	' THE LOW-TIME WARNING IS SILENT. There was a beep a second under ten, and
15875               	; 	' it was the wrong instrument for the job: the last ten seconds are the
15876               	; 	' busiest part of a round, so a repeating tone arrives exactly when the
15877               	; 	' player most needs to hear the hazards, and it fought the prize arpeggio
15878               	; 	' for channel 2 as well. The flash says the same thing and says it in the
15879               	; 	' place the player is already looking.
15880               	;
15881               	; 	' FOOTSTEPS ARE NOISE, AND ON THE NOISE CHANNEL -- testsounds variant A.
15882               	; 	'
15883               	; 	' They were two alternating TONES on channel 0, which is neither what the
15884               	; 	' original does nor a good use of a channel: the recording says a footstep
15885               	; 	' is a short burst of white noise, and channel 3 was sitting unused while
15886               	; 	' the footsteps and the jump sweep shared channel 0 and had to take turns.
15887               	; 	'
15888               	; 	' TESTSOUNDS RUN D: a SHORT tick at the measured RATE.
15889               	; 	'
15890               	; 	' The two dials are independent and both were tried at the bench. The
15891               	; 	' 2600 plays a 64 ms burst every 165 ms -- six a second -- and variant A
15892               	; 	' copies both. Ten a second was tried on the way here and reads as
15893               	; 	' hurrying rather than running. What D changes is not the cadence but the
15894               	; 	' TICK: two frames rather than four, and a notch louder to carry at half
15895               	; 	' the length. Same six a second, less of it.
15896               	; 	'
15897               	; 	' EIGHT A SECOND, AND THE ACCUMULATOR NOW CARRIES ITS REMAINDER.
15898               	; 	'
15899               	; 	' sfw counted pixels and the trigger did `sfw = 0`, THROWING AWAY whatever
15900               	; 	' was past the threshold. kspd is about four pixels a pass, so a threshold
15901               	; 	' of 17 did not fire at 17 -- it fired at the first multiple past it, about
15902               	; 	' 20, and every rate this was ever set to came out slower than the number
15903               	; 	' said: the "six a second" was 5.2 and the "ten" that read as hurrying was
15904               	; 	' really 8.7. Subtracting the threshold instead keeps the fraction, so the
15905               	; 	' rate is what it claims to be at any walking speed.
15906               	; 	'
15907               	; 	' MEASURED OFF THE COLECOVISION: 14 px, about 7.4 a second.
15908               	; 	'
15909               	; 	' It was 15 px and 6.9 a second, picked between an 8.0 that read as
15910               	; 	' slightly hurried and a 6.1 that read as trudging -- a judgement between
15911               	; 	' two other judgements, with nothing underneath it. The ColecoVision
15912               	; 	' recording settles it: footfalls land every 0.130 s across a twelve-second
15913               	; 	' continuous run, which is 7.7 a second, and that is the one finding in the
15914               	; 	' whole sound analysis the method resolves EXACTLY -- a rhythm rather than a
15915               	; 	' pitch, counted off the RMS track rather than inferred from a spectrum.
15916               	; 	' (colecosounds variant 1A; assets/sfx/sfxref-coleco.md has the working.)
15917               	; 	'
15918               	; 	' 104 px/s over 14 px is 7.43 a second. 13 px would give 8.00, and 7.7 sits
15919               	; 	' almost exactly between them -- so this is the nearer of the two, and it is
15920               	; 	' also the one that does not walk back into the 8.0 that was rejected by ear.
15921               	; 	'
15922               	; 	' WHY THE GAME KEEPS A DISTANCE AND THE BENCH KEEPS A CADENCE. The bench
15923               	; 	' plays a fixed eight frames between steps because it has no walking to tie
15924               	; 	' them to; the game accumulates PIXELS TRAVELLED, so the feet keep time with
15925               	; 	' the legs when he is slowed or stopped. Matching "7.4 a second" therefore
15926               	; 	' means matching it AT HIS WALKING SPEED, and assumes the ColecoVision's
15927               	; 	' crook walks at ours -- which the recording cannot confirm.
15928               	; 	'
15929               	; 	' The dial is this one constant and the subtraction below, which must stay
15930               	; 	' threshold + 1 or the carry is wrong.
15931               	; 	'
15932               	; 	' SOT = 2 IS THE SHORTEST TICK THERE IS, and 1 is SILENCE. The decay block
15933               	; 	' below runs LATER IN THE SAME sfx_tick, so a count of 1 is decremented to
15934               	; 	' zero on the pass that set it and the note-off fires before the sound has
15935               	; 	' lasted any time at all. 2 survives to the next pass, which is one pass of
15936               	; 	' sound -- about 42 ms against the bench's 33, as close as a per-pass timer
15937               	; 	' gets, and the reason the bench and the game cannot sound identical.
15938               	; 	'
15939               	; 	' Register 4 is white noise at the fastest rate.
15940               	; 	'
15941               	; 	' VOLUME 9, WHICH IS UNDER EVERYTHING ELSE ON PURPOSE. The hit, the prize
15942               	; 	' and the jump are 12 and 13, and they happen ONCE; footsteps play for the
15943               	; 	' whole round. At 13 they were level with the events they are supposed to
15944               	; 	' sit beneath, so the effects that carry information had nothing to stand
15945               	; 	' out from. The tone version was 7 for the same reason -- noise does read
15946               	; 	' quieter than a tone at the same number, which is why this is 9 and not

16144 FE0E C03A  30 	mov *r10+,r0
16145 FE10 0450  20 	b *r0
16146               	;
16147               	; 	' EVERYTHING BELOW THIS LINE IS ASSEMBLED INTO BANK 1, so the INCLUDE order
16148               	; 	' is load-bearing and nothing but data may follow it.
16149               	; 	'
16150               	; 	' THE FONT IS NOW IN THE BANK TOO, and it used to be deliberately outside:
16151               	; 	' keeping one readable thing in bank 0 means a bank-selection mistake shows
16152               	; 	' as "text survives, art does not" rather than a uniformly blank screen,
16153               	; 	' which is a genuinely useful thing to have when a bank goes wrong.
16154               	; 	'
16155               	; 	' THE FONT HAS A BANK OF ITS OWN, and the reason is not its size.
16156               	; 	'
16157               	; 	' Bank 1 was FULL -- six spare bytes of 8,192 -- which shut the door on
16158               	; 	' moving anything else out of the fixed area, and the fixed area is the
16159               	; 	' only budget that cannot be grown (linkticart writes exactly three
16160               	; 	' loader pages and discards the rest; they are the 32K expansion's RAM at
16161               	; 	' >A000, not cart ROM). A second bank costs a bigger cart -- five pages
16162               	; 	' round up to eight, so 32 KB becomes 64 KB -- and buys back the ability
16163               	; 	' to keep evacuating data out of code.
16164               	; 	'
16165               	; 	' THE FONT IS THE RIGHT TENANT because it is read ONCE. Two DEFINEs copy
16166               	; 	' it into VRAM at setup and nothing looks at it again, so it is the only
16167               	; 	' block here that can sit on a page which is not permanently mapped. See
16168               	; 	' setup_font: bank 2 is selected for those two statements and bank 1 for
16169               	; 	' the whole of the rest of the program.
16170               	; 	'
16171               	; 	' EVERYTHING ELSE STAYS IN BANK 1, because everything else is read during
16172               	; 	' play -- art on a screen crossing, templates on a band blit, the lookup
16173               	; 	' tables every pass. One permanently-mapped bank for all of it means
16174               	; 	' there is no switch to miss.
16175               	; 	#if TI994A
16176               	; 	BANK 2
16177      01EC     BANK_0_FREE:	EQU >fffe-$
     **** ****     > .rept

16651               	; 	' AND THE TITLE'S DISPLAY LIST, for the same reason as the font: walked
16652               	; 	' once by title_draw, at boot and on a return to the title, and never
16653               	; 	' during play. title_draw selects bank 2 around its walk.
16654               	; 	'
16655               	; 	' ITS MESSAGE BOXES DID NOT COME WITH IT. They are the same format and
16656               	; 	' were in the same generated file, which is what made this worth doing
16657               	; 	' carefully: they are walked when a ROUND ENDS, mid-game, so on bank 2
16658               	; 	' they would have returned bytes from the wrong page at the moment a life
16659               	; 	' is lost -- and with no error at build or run time. gentitle.py now
16660               	; 	' writes them to title.bas below, which stays in bank 1.
16661               	; 	INCLUDE "titledl.bas"
16662               	; 	' ==================================================
16663               	; 	' THE TITLE SCREEN, AS A DISPLAY LIST
16664               	; 	' Generated by assets/gentitle.py -- do not edit here.
16665               	; 	'
16666               	; 	' row, col, length, then `length` bytes; 255 ends.
16667               	; 	' Walked by title_draw only.
16668               	; 	'
16669               	; 	' LIVES IN BANK 2, with the fonts, because it is read ONCE
16670               	; 	' -- at boot and on a return to the title. title_draw
16671               	; 	' selects bank 2 around its walk and restores bank 1.
16672               	; 	' The message boxes in title.bas are the same format and
16673               	; 	' CANNOT come with it: they are read when a round ends.
16674               	; 	' ==================================================
16675               	;

18125               	; 	INCLUDE "store.bas"
18126               	; 	' Keystone Kapers store -- GENERATED by assets/genstore.py. Do not edit.
18127               	; 	'
18128               	; 	' EIGHT band templates of 5 rows x 32 cols (160 bytes each) plus a 32-byte
18129               	; 	' index over (level, screen). The whole 8-screen, 4-level building is about
18130               	; 	' 1.3 KB instead of the 5,120 bytes it would cost to store literally.
18131               	; 	'
18132               	; 	' All eight templates are ONE contiguous block under ONE label, so a band
18133               	; 	' blit is
18134               	; 	'     SCREEN stor_tpl, tpl*160, toprow*32, 32, 5, 32
18135               	; 	' with no label ladder -- SCREEN needs a literal label and a label cannot be
18136               	; 	' chosen by a variable, which is why RallyX needed a 4-way IF over its maze
18137               	; 	' tables. One block sidesteps it.
18138               	; 	'
18139               	; 	' 160 is EVEN, so this cannot leave the location counter odd and misalign
18140               	; 	' the word tables defined after it.
18141               	; 	'
18142               	; 	' template ids:
18143               	; 	'   0 T_AISLE_A
18144               	; 	'   1 T_AISLE_B
18145               	; 	'   2 T_ESC_W
18146               	; 	'   3 T_ESC_E
18147               	; 	'   4 T_ELEV
18148               	; 	'   5 T_ROOF0
18149               	; 	'   6 T_ROOF1
18150               	; 	'   7 T_ROOF2
18151               	; 	'   8 T_ROOF3
18152               	; 	'   9 T_ROOF4
18153               	; 	'   10 T_ROOF5
18154               	; 	'   11 T_ROOF6
18155               	; 	'   12 T_ROOF7
18156               	; 	'   13 T_END_W
18157               	; 	'   14 T_END_E
18158               	;
18159               	; stor_tpl:	' 15 templates x 160 bytes
18160               cvb_STOR_TPL
